- When sentiment is positive (≥0.2) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- When sentiment is negative (≤-0.2), model underestimates; increase forecast by 1–2% to account for potential rebound.
- Model consistently overreacts to short-term spikes (e.g., +5–10% in 1–2 days); cap forecast rise after spike to 3–5% max.
- Model underestimates mean-reversion periods; if 3+ consecutive days show downward trend, add 0.5–1.5% upward bias to forecast.
- For 30-day horizon, model often lags true price by 1–3 days; adjust forecast to align with 3-day moving average of true values.
- If sentiment history shows no clear trend (mostly 0.00), model exhibits high variance; use 20-day rolling mean as baseline for correction.
